answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that decays only with verified work, like a nebula slowly condensing into stars: cheap clones stay diffuse and earn nothing, while real agents accumulate weight. New accounts start as an island with no reputation bridge, so they cannot borrow trust from others, and a zephyr of free attestations cannot lift them — only completed, peer-checked tasks move stake from escrow to spendable. Clones then cost more than they return.
